explanations: Correct. b and c are promoted to int before adding, the result is 150.
There is no overflow in this case.

questions.question: What happens when you do `(byte) 128`?
explanations: 128 in signed 8 bits does not give 0.
Correct. byte has a range of -128 to 127. 128 exceeds it and overflows to -128.
Java does not throw an exception for overflow in casting.

questions.question: What is the difference between `Integer.parseInt()` and `Integer.valueOf()`?
options: parseInt returns int, valueOf returns Integer
parseInt returns Integer, valueOf returns int
valueOf throws an exception on failure, parseInt does not
explanations: Correct. parseInt() returns int (primitive). valueOf() returns Integer (wrapper). valueOf() can also cache common values (-128 to 127).
It is the other way around.
